newsitem.title: USA: Imation sees modest accretion from deal.
newsitem.headline: Imation sees modest accretion from deal.

text.p: Imation Corp expects its acquisition of privately held Cemax-Icon Inc to be modestly accretive to Imation earnings in 1998 and 1999, said Clifford Pinder, vice president of Medical Imaging Systems for Imation, on Wednesday.

In a conference call following the announcement of the acquisition, Pinder said, "In 1998 and 1999, we expect the acquisition of this business to be modestly accretive. Its part of our overall plan. If we look at the size of this business in the scope of a $2.3 billion company, in the near term, it's not going to add significant accretion to our total results."
Imation, spun off in July 1996 by Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co, reported 1996 revenues of $2.3 billion.

The maker of diagnostic imaging equipment, films for electronic and X-Ray imaging, and a variety of other products, said Wednesday it had agreed to acquire Cemax-Icon for an initial cash payment of $30 million. Additional payments of about $49 million will be paid over two years if certain milestones are achieved.

Imation said it will write off about $40 million in acquired in-process research and development in the deal. Excluding that one-time charge, Imation said it does not expect any material impact on 1997 results from the acquisition.
Fremont, Calif.,-based Cemax-Icon specializes in medical imaging and information management systems.
